lines.text: Rei has claimed the chair by the window, coat still on, her cup balanced on the armrest. On the low table between you sits the tin of biscuits you brought up from the shop below — plain, unglamorous, half open.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You tell her that even the biscuits probably need her approval before they're allowed in.
lines.source: I tease Rei that even the biscuits probably need her approval

lines.speaker: dilek-sahin
lines.text: They do, actually. I ran them through a short interview. The shortbread was evasive, but the ginger one had references.
She picks up the ginger biscuit and turns it over, examining it like a manuscript page.

lines.speaker: dilek-sahin
lines.text: For the record, the coffee rules are not a menu. They're a shortlist. There's a difference, and I'll defend it in writing if I have to.
She bites into the biscuit, unbothered, and looks back at you over the rim of her cup.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You admit that you didn't really come up for the coffee. You stayed because you wanted her company.
lines.source: I admit that I stayed for her company rather than the coffee

lines.text: She sets the cup down on the armrest, more carefully than it needs. When she speaks again her tone is level, but the dry edge has gone out of it.

lines.speaker: dilek-sahin
lines.text: That's a better reason than the coffee. I'd have said so sooner if you'd led with it.

lines.speaker: dilek-sahin
lines.text: I'm still deciding between the three films for Saturday. If you're around, you could help me argue about it. No obligation — I just don't trust my own taste this week.
